Here they are...

1. You read a two-line email from your manager five times, looking for what you did wrong.

2. You sit in the car park for a few minutes before you walk in, getting ready to be "on".

3. You say "no worries, I'll get it done" before you've checked whether you have time.

4. You eat lunch at your desk with one hand and answer messages with the other.

5. You lose your train of thought mid-sentence in a meeting and laugh it off.

6. You feel your chest tighten when your phone lights up after 6pm.

7. You leave at the end of the day and can't remember a single moment you enjoyed.

This is what high-functioning survival mode looks like at work.

You keep delivering. Your reviews are good. Everyone thinks you're coping. Underneath it, your body has been treating every message like an emergency for years.

I spent 17 years in corporate doing every one of these, and I called it being good at my job.

If this hit close to home, there's nothing wrong with you. You're not weak and you're not bad at your job. Your nervous system has been on alert for far too long.

Recognise: Notice which of these you did today, and where you felt it in your body.

Respond: Before you answer the next message, ask: is this urgent, or does it just feel urgent?

Release: Before you leave, write two lists, my tasks and their tasks. Leave the second list on the desk.

You don't have to quit your job to heal. It works step by step, right where you are.

You've read a hundred posts like this one.
Saved a few.
Changed nothing.

This one's different — it's the exact tool that helps you catch stress in the moment, before it becomes another year lost to burnout.

Less time spinning in the same loop.

Less money on things that don't touch the real problem.

Less energy wasted on stress that was never actually about what you thought it was.

It won't fix years overnight.

But it's the tool I wish I'd had three years ago — and it's yours in the next five minutes.

Comment TOOLKIT if this is the one you actually act on.♥️

#3RMethod #RecogniseRespondRelease #BurnoutRecovery #NervousSystemHealth #StressRegulation
